body: Could we remove this deduplication or key it by a provider supplied execution ID? Hyperliquid identifies each execution with the unique `tid`; `orderId + timestamp + size + price` is not documented as unique. With `aggregateByTime: false`, two legitimate fills can share those four values, and this branch now drops one before either individual display or aggregation, understating execution count, size, fee, and PnL. `origin/main` transforms the fetched fills directly, so this data loss is introduced by `flattenFills`. Please add a regression test with two same-order, same-millisecond, same price, same size fills and verify both remain represented.
action: Removed the dedupe entirely — no safe key exists without a provider execution id, and only the first page carries fills so it protected nothing; added a regression test with two identical fills that fails with the dedupe restored.

body: Could we base unaggregated row IDs on a stable provider execution identifier rather than `acc.length`? Adding a newer fill shifts the index of every existing row, so a refresh changes FlashList keys and can make the identifier passed to Activity Details resolve to no fill or the wrong fill. Hyperliquid exposes `tid` specifically as the unique trade ID; if the provider-neutral `OrderFill` model cannot carry it yet, we need a stable provider neutral execution ID before exposing individual fills. Please cover the case where a newer fill is prepended and existing execution IDs remain unchanged.
action: Unaggregated ids now come from fill content plus an occurrence index instead of acc.length, so a prepended newer fill leaves existing ids untouched; prepend-stability test added. OrderFill cannot carry `tid` yet — that is a Core change, noted in the reply.

body: Could we build this control with the existing `Checkbox` from `@metamask/design-system-react-native` so the interactive node has `accessibilityRole="checkbox"`? `ButtonBase` exposes button semantics, while React Native's `checked` state is defined for checkbox/radio roles; setting only `accessibilityState.checked` does not give assistive technology the checkbox contract. The current tests assert the raw prop but not the role. Please use the design-system primitive and assert both role and checked state.
action: Rebuilt on the design-system Checkbox with the pill styling applied via twClassName/labelProps; both tests assert accessibilityRole 'checkbox' and the checked state. Flagged the DS primitive's fixed 22px box to the designer.

body: Suggestion: replace the third positional boolean with an options object and an explicit mode such as `fillDisplay: 'aggregated' | 'individual'`. Calls such as `usePerpsActivityQuery(accountId, enabled, false)` hide the meaning at the call site and allow future invalid boolean combinations. A named options type makes the state space explicit and follows TypeScript's preference for inference friendly object APIs and modeled domain states.
action: Third parameter is now UsePerpsActivityQueryOptions with fillDisplay: 'aggregated' | 'individual'; both call sites and their tests updated.

body: Unaggregated fills fail details lookup (High Severity): Turning Aggregated off rebuilds trade rows with per-fill ids, but Activity Details still rematches through `usePerpsActivityQuery` with `aggregateFills` defaulting to true. Those ids do not line up with the collapsed order row, so tapping an individual execution opens a not-found details screen, or in the first-row collision case shows the combined order instead of that fill.
action: Already fixed in a23bb80115 on an earlier round and replied to on the thread; no second reply posted.

body: Individual fill opens aggregated details (Medium Severity): Resolving against the aggregated list first can open the combined order when the user tapped a single execution. Both views build ids as `orderId-timestamp-index`, so the newest fill of the newest order always shares the aggregated row id and shows combined size, fees, and PnL.
action: Already fixed in 707e36971e on an earlier round and replied to on the thread; no second reply posted.
